annotations.text:
Reading depth is the bridge.

Plain / Study / Scholar changes only what opens by DEFAULT — never what is available. A layman who gets curious expands the same scholarly views a student reads. One content set, two audiences.

Try the toggle.

Peek before you leap.

Click 20:110 in the plain-English paragraph. A link never navigates on first touch — you get the verse, its translation, and WHY it is linked. Most link-following should end here, without ever leaving the page.

Ikhtilāf is reported, not resolved.

Three readings of Kursī, each with who held it, the evidence, and a locator. Weight of support is shown by the left rule and the badge — majority, reported, minority — never by hiding the minority.

Every link names a scholar.

Links come from what a mufassir actually cites while commenting — not from similarity search. That is why the peek card's footer can always say who drew the connection, and why a link is reviewable like any other claim.

What 'clean' rules out.

No permanent sidebar. No tab bar of eight tafsīr works. No verse cards in a feed. No streaks or badges. Structure carried by type and space, not boxes — except the one boundary that is non-negotiable: our summary never looks like a scholar's words.

One engine, two axes — this one is live.

Click any ground and any accent. All 32 combinations come from a single hue value: lightness and chroma are fixed per role, so every accent clears contrast on every ground by construction, not by luck. No skin files to maintain.

The grounds borrow the accent's hue at very low chroma — a chosen neutral, not an inherited grey.

The accent never touches the Qur'an.

Switch to Red or Purple and watch: the Arabic and the translation do not move off full-contrast ink. The accent lives in chrome, links, the summary rule and focus. A 'purple theme' must never mean purple scripture.

Editions differ in letters, not fonts.

Compare the four bismillah samples — Uthmani carries the alef wasla and superscript alef, IndoPak follows South Asian conventions. That is orthography, so it is a text edition, not a font setting. The font is chosen separately.

Why the mushaf page is its own view.

Page-perfect Madinah rendering uses one font file per page — 604 of them — where each glyph is a whole word. It cannot reflow, resize freely or be searched. A tafsīr column needs all three, so the printed page gets its own screen instead.

Per-ayah files make single-ayah exact.

Recitations come one file per ayah, so 'play this ayah only' needs no seeking inside a surah-length track — no drift, no clipped endings. Packs download by juz (~28 MB) rather than whole-Qur'an (~1 GB).

Auto-advance ships OFF.
